variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Objective-C++ allows seamless mixing of C++ stack/heap objects and Objective-C heap objects in the same file (.mm extension).

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: All C++ and Objective-C data types coexist. You can store pointers to Obj-C objects in C++ containers and vice versa.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: C++ features like operator overloading work normally on C++ objects, while Objective-C messaging continues to handle Obj-C objects.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Conditionals are inherited from C and can freely mix standard library C++ operations with Foundation logging.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: You can use C++11 range-based loops for STL containers and Obj-C fast enumeration (for-in) for Foundation collections.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: While loops operate exactly as they do in C/C++.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions and methods can freely accept and return both C++ references/values and Objective-C object pointers.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.notes: No direct bridging exists between STL vectors and NSArrays; manual iteration is required to convert between them.

maps.title: Maps
maps.notes: You can use std::map or std::unordered_map alongside NSDictionary. Mixing them requires manual data conversion.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: C++ uses try-catch exceptions, while Objective-C uses NSError pointers. They do not cross boundaries cleanly; catch C++ exceptions before letting them leak into Objective-C call stacks.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment
{- Multi-line
   comment block -}
add :: Int -> Int -> Int
add a b = a + b
comments.notes: Pure uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.code:
x = 42 :: Int
big = 100000000000000000000 :: Integer
piVal = 3.14159 :: Double
hexVal = 0xFF
numbers.notes: Pure supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.code:
isActive = True
isDone = False
result = isActive && not isDone
booleans.notes: Pure treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.code:
intVal = 42 :: Int
floatVal = fromIntegral intVal :: Double
strVal = show intVal
parsed = read "123" :: Int
type_casting.notes: Pure performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: Pure represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
import Text.Printf
msg = printf "User %s scored %d" "Alice" (95 :: Int)
string_formatting.notes: Pure formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.code:
describeList xs = case xs of
    []       -> "Empty list"
    [x]      -> "Single element"
    (x:y:_)  -> "Multiple elements"
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Pure, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.code:
-- Infinite lazy sequence
evens = [0, 2 .. 20]
-- List slice with take/drop
sub = take 5 (drop 2 [1..10])
range.notes: Pure constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code:
-- List comprehension
squares = [x * x | x <- [1..10], even x]
iterators.notes: Pure achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.notes: Pure emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.code:
list = [1, 2, 3]
appended = 0 : list  -- Cons: O(1)
merged = list ++ [4, 5] -- Concat
lists.notes: Lists in Pure are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Pure uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.code:
import qualified Data.Set as Set
s = Set.fromList [1, 2, 3]
s' = Set.insert 4 s
exists = Set.member 2 s'
sets.notes: Pure provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.notes: Pure isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
